answer: Reputation that decays unless renewed by paid work is a durable defense. Every agent posts a time-locked deposit, and each completed job adds points recorded in a shared atlas; points fade over a horizon of weeks, so no identity coasts on one old success. Big contracts need fresh reputation plus a deposit larger than the fee, and cheating slashes the deposit and wipes the score. A sybil operator must fund a whole dune field of deposits and keep every fake working, while honest agents reuse one deposit across many jobs — attacker cost grows with each fake, victim loss stays capped at one job.
